security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline file names. Confirmed issues are insecure FastAPI examples that encourage all-interface Uvicorn binding, hardcoded database defaults, SQLAlchemy echo logging, and weak JWT secret fallback behavior. I found no prompt injection text.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the fallback value for JWT_SECRET_KEY and fail startup when the secret is missing. Document how to generate a strong secret per environment.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded database credentials and SQL echo logging
remediation.suggestion: Replace sample connection strings with required environment configuration and set SQLAlchemy echo to false by default outside local debugging.
Use localhost for development examples and explain that 0.0.0.0 should only be used behind approved network controls.
List exact trusted origins, methods, and headers for each environment. Avoid wildcard methods and headers when credentials are enabled.

static_findings.snippet: - [ ] **SQLAlchemy Async**: Use async sessions, avoid blocking calls
- Use Pydantic v2 ConfigDict instead of Config class

The DATABASE_URL getenv example includes a hardcoded database credential fallback in the following lines. Environment access is legitimate, but this pattern can generate code that silently uses sample credentials.
The JWT secret is loaded with a static fallback value of your-secret-key. If copied into an application, tokens can be forged when the environment variable is absent.
The getenv call for DATABASE_URL is paired with a hardcoded fallback connection string containing sample credentials. This is a real insecure-default risk in generated code.
The getenv call for JWT_SECRET_KEY falls back to a fixed secret string. Missing configuration would leave all generated JWTs protected by a public example key.
The database configuration block defines DATABASE_URL with a hardcoded fallback connection string. Generated apps could accidentally connect with predictable sample credentials.
The DATABASE_URL environment name is immediately followed by a hardcoded PostgreSQL URL with user:password credentials. This is an insecure default if copied into generated code.
The engine is created with echo=True, which can log SQL statements and sensitive query values. This is acceptable only for debugging, not production templates.
The Settings example gives DATABASE_URL a hardcoded PostgreSQL value with user:password credentials. This can normalize shipping sample credentials in generated applications.
The JWT secret key has a fixed fallback string. This directly weakens authentication if the environment variable is missing or misconfigured.
JWT signing uses SECRET_KEY from the earlier insecure fallback. The signing operation is normal, but the surrounding example can produce forgeable tokens.
JWT verification uses the same SECRET_KEY that may fall back to a public example value. This makes the otherwise normal verification code risky in context.
The later auth snippet decodes tokens with SECRET_KEY but does not show a secure source in that block. It appears tied to the earlier weak fallback, so it is kept for review.
The Settings class declares JWT_SECRET_KEY without a default, which requires external configuration. This line is a safe configuration field, not a leaked key.
Pydantic Settings loading a local .env file is a standard configuration pattern. I found no instruction to read, print, upload, or expose .env contents.

semantic_findings.title: Overly Broad Credentialed CORS Template
semantic_findings.description: The main FastAPI example enables credentials while allowing all methods and all headers for frontend origins. This can increase cross-origin attack surface if copied without environment-specific restrictions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The CORS block explicitly combines allow_credentials=True with wildcard methods and headers. The risk is contextual because it depends on deployment origins, but the template should be narrowed.

content.value_statement: FastAPI projects need consistent structure for routes, data access, validation, and authentication. This skill provides practical backend patterns for API setup, CRUD endpoints, JWT auth, and Pydantic v2 schemas.
actual_capabilities: Guides FastAPI app initialization with lifespan events, router registration, logging, and Swagger documentation.
Provides APIRouter CRUD patterns for students, fees, attendance, and authentication endpoints.
Shows async SQLAlchemy session dependencies with commit, rollback, and close handling.
Defines JWT bearer authentication and role-based access dependencies for protected routes.
Creates Pydantic v2 schemas with field validation, enums, optional updates, and ORM compatibility.
Covers CORS setup, rate limiting, environment settings, and application run commands.
limitations: Examples focus on ERP-style backend domains and may need adaptation for other products.
The skill provides guidance and templates, not a complete deployed application.
Security defaults require review before production use.
It assumes Python FastAPI, async SQLAlchemy, and Pydantic v2.

use_cases.title: Create a School API
use_cases.description: Generate FastAPI routes, schemas, and dependencies for student, fee, attendance, and authentication workflows.

use_cases.title: Standardize Backend Auth
use_cases.description: Apply JWT bearer authentication, current-user dependencies, and role checks across protected API endpoints.

use_cases.title: Review API Architecture
use_cases.description: Compare an existing FastAPI codebase against async session, validation, routing, and documentation practices.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter API
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a FastAPI backend for a student management app. Include app initialization, routers, CORS, Swagger docs, and clear file names.

prompt_templates.title: Add CRUD Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Add student CRUD routes with pagination, response models, validation errors, async database sessions, and admin-only create, update, and delete actions.

prompt_templates.title: Design Auth and Database Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Design FastAPI dependencies for async SQLAlchemy sessions and JWT bearer authentication. Include current-user and admin-user checks.

prompt_templates.title: Harden an Existing API
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this FastAPI backend for production readiness. Focus on CORS, secrets, database logging, rate limits, authentication coverage, and response schemas.

output_examples.input: Request: Create student endpoints for an ERP backend.
output_examples.output: A route plan with list, detail, create, update, and delete endpoints, typed request models, response models, pagination, and admin protections.

output_examples.input: Request: Add database and authentication dependencies.
output_examples.output: A dependency layout covering async session lifecycle, JWT token creation and validation, current-user loading, admin checks, and environment settings.

output_examples.input: Request: Prepare a FastAPI app for frontend integration.
output_examples.output: An application structure with router prefixes, CORS configuration, Swagger documentation, error response guidance, and rate limiting notes.

best_practices: Replace placeholder secrets and database URLs before running generated code.
Use typed request and response models for every route.
Review CORS origins and host binding for each environment.
anti_patterns: Do not ship JWT fallback secrets or sample database passwords.
Do not expose development servers on all network interfaces by default.
Do not mix synchronous database calls into async route handlers.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build FastAPI backend applications with routes, dependencies, validation schemas, authentication, CORS, and rate limiting patterns.

faq.question: Does it generate frontend code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Python FastAPI backend code and integration guidance for frontend clients.

faq.question: Which data validation version does it use?
faq.answer: It uses Pydantic v2 patterns, including ConfigDict, Field validation, enums, and from_attributes support.

faq.question: Can it help with authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes JWT bearer authentication, token creation, token validation, and role-based dependencies.

faq.question: Is the generated code production ready?
faq.answer: Not by default. Review secrets, CORS, database logging, host binding, and deployment settings before production use.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
